clue.text: Alter charts to gain advantage

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: turn round the tables, tables being charts of figures
second meaning: the idiom for reversing a situation so the loser comes out on top

explanation.surface: Someone fiddles the charts to get ahead of their rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is the phrase read word by word: to turn is to alter, and tables are charts.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to reverse a position so that a former underdog now has the upper hand over an opponent.

clue.text: Deceitful, having less than thirteen cards

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read cryptically: a bridge hand is thirteen cards, so fewer is under a hand

explanation.surface: A card cheat is caught holding a short hand.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge each player is dealt thirteen cards, which make up a hand; the word split as UNDER HAND describes holding fewer.
explanation.definitionFit: Underhand dealing is secret and dishonest, a standard synonym for sly or deceitful conduct.

clue.text: Sun editor upset by Page 3 girls?

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: the usual abbreviation for an editor

explanation.surface: The Sun's editor is in trouble over the paper's famous topless models.
explanation.walkthrough: Page 3 of the Sun, a British tabloid, long carried photographs of topless women; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Page 3 models posed unclothed for the tabloid, so they are an example of people photographed without clothes.

clue.text: Astronomer uses aperture to frame galaxy finally

indicators.note: a frame surrounds a picture, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: an aperture is an opening or gap

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word just before it

explanation.surface: An astronomer peers through a telescope opening to bring a galaxy into view.
explanation.walkthrough: Fred Hoyle was the British astronomer who coined the term Big Bang.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Fred Hoyle was a celebrated twentieth-century British scientist who studied stars and cosmology.

clue.text: Moving magnet attracts rat and shrew

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift position and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: A moving magnet seems to pull in a rat and a shrew, like a science demonstration gone wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrew' looks like another small animal beside the rat, but it means a scolding woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a harsh, quarrelsome woman, the same sense as shrew in The Taming of the Shrew.

clue.text: Tramp's trousers may have to stop falling before rising
I laze around, says this fair lady

indicators.note: letters moved around are scattered and set down in another order

explanation.surface: A lady admits she lounges about idly all day.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliza Doolittle is the heroine of the musical My Fair Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: The flower girl Eliza Doolittle is the central character of the Lerner and Loewe musical based on Pygmalion.

clue.text: Everyone at home with wine, women and song? Wait!

parts.note: the classic recipe for enjoying oneself

explanation.surface: Everyone is at home enjoying a party of drink, company and music, when someone calls for patience.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase urges patience, telling someone that a thing will happen eventually when the right moment arrives.

clue.text: Officer's three-wheeler, which stops all people working

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for the noun it describes

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: An army officer rides about on a tricycle.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive of the officer supplies the S that joins the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage in which workers across all industries walk out together halts the whole workforce at once.

clue.text: Woman on time for March 25

parts.note: a day is a period of time; on places it after

explanation.surface: A woman arrives punctually for an appointment in late March.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down-style reading 'on' just means following; Lady Day is the Feast of the Annunciation and an English quarter day.
explanation.definitionFit: The Feast of the Annunciation of the Virgin Mary falls on that date and was traditionally an English rent quarter day.

clue.text: Step on board with real tin mixture

indicators.note: a mixture blends its ingredients together into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone boards a vessel carrying a blend of genuine metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' means aboard a ship, not on a plank.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratlines are the small ropes tied across a sailing ship's shrouds, forming rungs that sailors climb like a ladder.

clue.text: Fiery Welsh lord died in Iris's embrace

indicators.note: to be in someone's embrace is to be held inside their arms

parts.note: the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered Welsh nobleman expires in the arms of a woman called Iris.
explanation.walkthrough: Idris is a giant of Welsh legend, whose seat is the mountain Cadair Idris.
explanation.definitionFit: In Welsh legend the giant Idris was a warrior prince, remembered in the name of the mountain Cadair Idris.

clue.text: Fancy the parcel being returned with zero charge!

indicators.note: a parcel being returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a bale is a bundle of goods
zero looks like the letter O
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted that sending back a parcel costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' reads as an exclamation of surprise, but it is the adjective meaning ornate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elaborate is intricate and ornamented, which is what a fancy design or decoration is.

clue.text: Understand first part of government file

indicators.note: the first part of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a rasp is a coarse file for wood or metal

explanation.surface: Someone tries to make sense of the opening section of an official government dossier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'File' suggests a folder of papers, but here it is the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp an idea is to take hold of it mentally, a common synonym for comprehending it.

clue.text: Drier subsequently found in kitbag

indicators.note: something found in a bag sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a pack is a kitbag, carried on the back

explanation.surface: Something to dry with turns up afterwards in a soldier's bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drier' looks like a comparative adjective but is a noun: something for drying.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack holding washed plates upright lets them drain and dry, so it serves as a drier for crockery.

clue.text: Thus a father gets time in "EastEnders", perhaps

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A dad lands a stint as an actor on a popular TV drama.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running BBC television serial set in London's East End; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: EastEnders is an example of a long-running serial television drama about the everyday lives of a community.

clue.text: Motor, scratched outside, needed by a golfer?

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the thing a golfer needs

indicators.note: one word placed outside another wraps around it

explanation.surface: A golfer's car has been scraped in the club car park.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers record the number of strokes taken at each hole on a printed card carried round the course.

clue.text: Deal with china when cooking food in Mexico

indicators.note: ingredients being cooked are mixed and transformed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook has to handle the crockery while making a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican dish of a rolled tortilla with a filling, covered in chilli sauce.

clue.text: Single man exposed as nonconformist

parts.note: an odd one is single, without a partner
exposed or revealed is out, as a secret is

explanation.surface: An unmarried man is revealed to be a rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the one person who differs from everyone else in a group, refusing to fit in.

clue.text: Sews loosely but exact, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so the word is judged by how it is said

parts.note: to exact is to demand payment, to levy

explanation.surface: A tailor stitches loosely but precisely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exact' looks like the adjective meaning precise, but it is the verb meaning to demand.
explanation.definitionFit: To tack fabric is to stitch it with long temporary stitches that hold it in place before proper sewing.

clue.text: Crown action needed for proof of ownership

parts.note: a crown is a championship title, as a boxer's

explanation.surface: A legal action is required to establish that the monarch owns something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crown' suggests the monarchy, but it is a sporting title.
explanation.definitionFit: This legal document records who holds the rights to a property, serving as evidence that it belongs to them.

clue.text: Instruct a stepchild to show discrimination

indicators.note: the letters are on show inside the run of words, needing only to be picked out

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the third

explanation.surface: A parent is told to teach a stepchild good judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is the ability to judge quality and discern what is fine or appropriate, as in discriminating judgement.

clue.text: Fool, about 50, with two in the bar

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A foolish fifty-year-old sits in a pub with a couple of companions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, but it is a bar of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Duple time in music has two main beats in each measure, as in a march.

clue.text: One making an attempt with a new start as an advertiser

indicators.note: a new start means the opening letter is swapped for a different one

explanation.surface: Someone makes a fresh attempt at a career in advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letter of the attempter's word is changed to C; a town crier announced news and notices in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A town crier called out public announcements and notices, so he advertised news to everyone in earshot.

clue.text: Famous person gets honour regardless

indicators.note: split as regard-less, it asks for a word meaning regard to be taken away

parts.note: to celebrate someone is to honour them
to regard is to rate or esteem

explanation.surface: A famous person is given an award whatever their merits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regardless' must be split into regard and less; the second half removes the first from the honouring word.
explanation.definitionFit: Celeb is the informal clipped form of celebrity, a well-known figure in the public eye.

clue.text: Mother's car, one that's eye-catching?

definitions.note: a clause standing for the thing that catches the eye

parts.note: ma is mother, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: Mum's car is a real head-turner.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: make-up applied to the eyes literally catches them.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is cosmetic applied to the eyelashes, drawing attention to the eyes and making them striking.

clue.text: "A Fish Called Jackson", reportedly

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound counts

parts.note: Jackson Pollock was the American drip painter

explanation.surface: A spoof film title on the comedy A Fish Called Wanda.
explanation.walkthrough: The surname of the painter Jackson Pollock is pronounced the same as the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The pollack is an edible sea fish of the cod family found in North Atlantic waters.

clue.text: Yankee in bed calling for doctor: irregular pulse

indicators.note: irregular means out of order, so the letters are set in a different sequence

explanation.surface: A sick American in bed summons a doctor because his heartbeat is erratic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' plays as a heartbeat, but pulses are edible seeds such as beans and lentils.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are the dried edible seeds of legumes, and this bean is a common variety used in chilli.
